nonLabourLines.description: Legacy Oracle data migration tooling / read licenses

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is based purely on backlog scope and rate card, not past velocity or cost performance.

Story points given (Fibonacci-like scale) are treated as relative sizing; unestimated items were sized by analogy to similarly-scoped, pointed tasks (e.g. PW-2 component library ~ sized like PW-5/PW-13; PW-8 legacy migration sized larger due to 400k/2M record volume and schema-mapping risk; PW-18 admin back-office sized like a medium CRUD feature).

1 story point is assumed to be roughly equivalent to 6-7 hours of combined delivery effort (dev+test), adjusted per task based on which roles are actually involved (e.g. PW-8 migration is backend+devops heavy with little frontend; PW-15 accessibility is frontend+QA heavy).

Backend Developer capacity is 1.5 FTE (~120 hrs/week team capacity at 40 hrs/week/FTE); allocated 900 hours implies roughly 7.5 weeks of dedicated backend capacity, which is reasonable for the backend-heavy items (auth, RBAC, payments, migration, audit log) but this role is the primary bottleneck for the plan.

Frontend Developer is only 1.0 FTE; 760 hours (~19 weeks solo) covers dashboard, invoice UI, design system, accessibility, responsive layout and admin UI. This role is thinly staffed relative to the number of UI-heavy backlog items and is flagged as a scheduling risk, not just a cost one.

QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE (24 hrs/week) is allocated 380 hours (~16 weeks); QA is scoped to test the Urgent/High items plus a pass on Medium items, with Low-priority items (support tickets, admin back-office, usage analytics, contract tests, decommission) getting lighter QA coverage proportional to their priority.

DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE (16 hrs/week) is allocated 180 hours (~11 weeks), covering CI/staging setup, migration infra support, observability, and rate-limiting infra work; this role is also thinly staffed and is treated as a shared/part-time resource across the project timeline rather than dedicated to any single sprint.

PW-2 (design system), PW-4 (RBAC), PW-6 (invoice list/detail), PW-8 (legacy migration), PW-10 (audit log), PW-14 (multi-currency), PW-16 (performance hardening), PW-18 (admin back-office), PW-20 (responsive layout), PW-22 (observability), PW-24 (decommission) are unestimated in points and were sized by the estimator using analogy to comparable pointed tasks; treat these hours as lower-confidence than the pointed items.

Non-labour costs are rough external/tooling estimates (Stripe sandbox/fees, Oracle migration tooling or read-license costs, a third-party accessibility audit, and first-year observability SaaS tooling) and do not include ongoing run-rate/hosting costs beyond year one.

Scenario spread (Low -16.7%, High +20% versus Most Likely) reflects the mix of well-understood pointed work (tighter variance) and the unestimated/analogy-sized and higher-risk items such as legacy data migration, multi-currency and RBAC (wider variance), plus general estimation uncertainty given the lack of historical actuals.

Estimate assumes the team works largely sequentially per priority (Urgent and blocking infra like CI/staging first) with some parallelism across roles, and does not include cost for a dedicated project manager or product owner role since none is listed on the rate card.

Low-priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) are included in the Most Likely estimate but are the first candidates for descoping if budget needs to shrink, as reflected in the reductions below.
input.reasoning: Sizing approach: pointed backlog items were converted to hours using an approximate 6-7 hours-per-point ratio, split across roles according to the nature of the work (e.g., payment integration and RBAC are backend+QA heavy; accessibility and responsive layout are frontend+QA heavy; CI/staging and observability are DevOps-heavy). Unestimated items were sized by analogy to comparable pointed items, with extra hours added for known high-risk items like the legacy Oracle migration (large data volumes, schema mapping, reconciliation risk) and multi-currency (FX handling, settlement correctness). Role hour totals were then checked for proportionality against each role's FTE capacity: Backend Developer (1.5 FTE) carries the largest share as the bulk of the backlog is API/business-logic work; Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) and QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) are allocated enough hours to cover UI and testing across all in-scope items but are flagged as capacity-constrained; DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) is kept to infrastructure-specific tasks only (CI/staging, migration support, observability, rate-limiting infra) consistent with its low availability. Non-labour costs cover the external/tooling spend implied by specific backlog items (Stripe, Oracle migration tooling, an external accessibility audit, and observability SaaS). Three scenarios (P20/P50/P80) were built around the Most Likely total, widening for the unestimated/high-risk items and lack of historical actuals, and verified via check_estimate to reconcile exactly with the underlying line items. Priority breakdown allocates each labour/non-labour line's cost to the priority of its associated backlog item(s), giving a rough view of where the budget concentrates (a large share sits in High and Medium priority work, with Urgent items like auth and payments being cost-concentrated but comparatively few in number).

reductions.description: Descope or defer all five Low-priority items (PW-12 support ticket submission, PW-18 admin back-office, PW-19 usage analytics, PW-23 helpdesk contract tests, PW-24 legacy decommission) to a later phase.
reductions.effect: Removes the full Low-priority allocation from labour lines (reduces Backend, Frontend, QA and DevOps hours proportionally); no impact on Urgent/High items needed to launch the core portal.

reductions.description: Reduce Multi-currency support (PW-14) to a single-currency (USD) launch and defer EUR/PLN support and daily FX handling to a follow-up release.
reductions.effect: Cuts backend and QA hours associated with FX rate integration, settlement logic and currency-specific test cases; simplifies invoice/payment reconciliation for launch.

reductions.description: Narrow the WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility pass (PW-15) to the highest-traffic screens (login, dashboard, invoice list) at launch, deferring full-portal coverage and the external audit.
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend/QA hours on lower-traffic screens and defers the third-party accessibility audit non-labour cost; full AA compliance is completed in a subsequent iteration.

reductions.description: Phase the legacy data migration (PW-8): migrate active/recent customer accounts and invoices first, defer historical archive records to a second migration batch after go-live.
reductions.effect: Cuts backend and DevOps migration/tooling hours and the associated Oracle tooling non-labour cost in the initial phase; reduces go-live risk window but requires a follow-up migration project.

reductions.description: Defer Observability (PW-22) dashboards/alerting beyond the payment path to a post-launch iteration; ship only payment-path tracing at launch.
reductions.effect: Reduces DevOps hours and defers part of the observability SaaS tooling non-labour cost; broader tracing/dashboards added once core flows are stable in production.
